page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the Eadv6 series, executing on the x86_64 AMD processor platform under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs. It utilizes a constrained-core configuration based on a 96-vCPU footprint, directing full host memory and local I/O capacity to a reduced processor count.

Memory allocation stands at 672.0 GB of RAM, delivering 14.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features bundled local NVMe SSD capacity measuring 5,670 GB, alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

The constrained vCPU ratio provides high memory-to-core density, reducing per-core licensing expenses for enterprise database engines while providing extensive physical memory and high-capacity local scratch storage. A notable tradeoff is the reduction in raw multi-threaded compute throughput relative to full-chassis configurations. The server fits memory-intensive relational databases, large in-memory caching systems, transactional systems with substantial temporary table footprints, and enterprise analytics workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered on the x86_64 AMD processor architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. Featuring a constrained vCPU profile, the instance allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory density of 14.0 GB per virtual processor. Storage infrastructure includes 5,670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity as well as compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. This resource distribution makes the instance cost-effective for software deployments bound by per-core database licensing models that still demand substantial memory allocations and rapid local temporary disk operations. The system is suited for enterprise relational database management systems, in-memory analytical datastores, and large-scale data transformation pipelines requiring significant RAM alongside high-capacity local temporary NVMe storage.
